children: , a supplier of cloud and AI networking equipment, faces a two-part test Tuesday: deliver more revenue and show how much profit that growth can generate. Shares fell 0.53% to $167.96 at 10:15 a.m. ET on November 2 as investors looked ahead to its November 3 results. AI demand could lift shipments, but the payoff depends on margins.

TipRanks' November 2 preview highlighted BofA's continued Buy rating ahead of the release. Arista's August guidance called for approximately $3.3 billion in third-quarter revenue and a 48%49% adjusted operating margin, compared with second-quarter revenue of $3.0357 billion and a 49.9% margin. That points to roughly 8.7% sequential revenue growth, alongside a 1.4-percentage-point margin decline at the guidance midpoint. Product mix and spending could determine how much of that extra revenue reaches operating profit.

The GuruFocus snapshot gives Arista a 99/100 GF Score, with strong readings across profitability, growth, financial strength and momentum. Yet a price-to-earnings ratio of 52.95 suggests investors already expect plenty from the business. Tuesday's hurdle could therefore extend beyond a revenue beat: stronger sales paired with resilient margins would offer a more convincing case for that valuation than growth accompanied by weaker profitability.

title: Arista Networks Stocks Move Lower With Earnings Testing Growth Against Margin Guidance
